You can pass a list of valid digits along with an 'invalid_audio_url', which will be played back at the beginning of each prompt. Playback will be interrupted when a DTMF signal is received. The `Answer command must be issued before the `gather_using_audio` command.

**Expected Webhooks (see [callback schema](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/call-control/gather-using-audio#callbacks) below):**

- `call.playback.started`
- `call.playback.ended`
- `call.dtmf.received` (you may receive many of these webhooks)
- `call.gather.ended`
data.summary_suggestion: Collect DTMF input with audio playback
data.description_suggestion: Plays an audio file on the call and collects DTMF (touch-tone) digits from the caller to build interactive voice menus. Specify valid DTMF digits to accept and optionally provide an invalid_audio_url to replay if the caller enters an invalid digit. Audio playback stops when a valid DTMF signal is received. Requires the call to be answered first. Returns results via `call.gather.ended` webhook with collected digits. Playback events are reported via `call.playback.started`, `call.playback.ended`, and `call.dtmf.received` webhooks.
data.reasoning: Original summary 'Gather using audio' is too vague. Description mentions 'invalid_audio_url' but doesn't clearly explain its purpose (replayed on invalid input). Missing clarity on what DTMF signals are collected, how they're validated, and the complete webhook flow. Enhanced version clarifies the interactive menu use case, DTMF validation mechanism, and all webhook events for better AI agent interpretability.

data.current_description:
Convert text to speech and play it on the call until the required DTMF signals are gathered to build interactive menus.

You can pass a list of valid digits along with an 'invalid_payload', which will be played back at the beginning of each prompt. Speech will be interrupted when a DTMF signal is received. The `Answer` command must be issued before the `gather_using_speak` command.

Speech playback stops when a valid DTMF signal is received. Requires the call to be answered first. Returns collected digits via `call.gather.ended` webhook. DTMF input events are reported via `call.dtmf.received` webhooks.

This operation is typically used to handle call routing changes, transfer scenarios, or to remove calls that should no longer wait in queue. Expected webhooks and state changes depend on the queue configuration and subsequent call control actions.

data.current_description:
Play an audio file on the call. If multiple play audio commands are issued consecutively,
the audio files will be placed in a queue awaiting playback.

*Notes:*

- When `overlay` is enabled, `target_legs` is limited to `self`.
- A customer cannot Play Audio with `overlay=true` unless there is a Play Audio with `overlay=false` actively playing.

**Expected Webhooks (see [callback schema](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/call-control/start-call-playback#callbacks) below):**

- `call.playback.started`
- `call.playback.ended`
data.description_suggestion: Plays an audio file from a specified URL on the call. Multiple consecutive playback commands queue audio files for sequential playback. Supports overlay mode for mixing audio with ongoing conversation (limited to `self` target leg). Overlay playback requires an active non-overlay playback to be playing. Returns `call.playback.started` webhook when playback begins and `call.playback.ended` webhook when playback completes. Audio files are played to specified call legs or all participants depending on target configuration.

data.current_description:

**Expected Webhooks (see [callback schema](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/call-control/stop-call-playback#callbacks) below):**

data.summary_suggestion: Stop active audio playback on call
data.description_suggestion: Stops any active audio playback on the call immediately, including audio files or text-to-speech output. This operation terminates playback and clears any queued audio files awaiting playback. Triggers either `call.playback.ended` webhook (for audio file playback) or `call.speak.ended` webhook (for text-to-speech playback) depending on the type of audio being stopped. The call remains active after playback stops.
